transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, what brought me in is that... I find myself checking things repeatedly. Like the same boxes, my lists, the drawers around our condo. I just check them over and over before I can move on to whatever I'm doing. 

The thing is, I know perfectly well I already looked. But I keep doing it anyway. My wife will be standing there waiting for me, telling me to just leave it be, but... well, it's just getting hard to stop doing it. So, that's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself having repeated, unwanted thoughts that bother you, or do you feel driven to perform certain actions other than checking things?

Well, yes, I do. I keep getting these... nagging thoughts, I guess you could call them. I'll start worrying that I might have accidentally thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box somewhere. 

I tell myself it's highly unlikely, but... well, the thought just comes back anyway. It just makes it very hard to sit down and settle.
Besides checking things repeatedly, do you find yourself doing any other actions over and over again, like washing your hands, counting, or arranging items in a certain way?

No, not really. I don't wash my hands any more than usual, and I don't count things or... line them up in any special way. It really is just the checking. Just going through the boxes and drawers over and over to make sure I didn't lose anything.
Do you find yourself saving items you don't really need or want, or having trouble getting rid of things, even if they seem unimportant to others?

No, not at all. I don't really hold onto things I don't need. My wife and I actually downsized to this condo a few years back, so we got rid of quite a bit then. I don't have any trouble throwing away junk mail or old newspapers or anything like that. It's just the worry that I might have accidentally tossed something I *did* need, which is why I keep going back to check. But I'm certainly not hoarding things.
Do you ever have intrusive thoughts about harming someone, or fears that you might accidentally cause harm, like leaving the stove on or the door unlocked?

No, I don't have thoughts like that. I don't worry about hurting anyone, and I don't really worry about the stove or the locks. I mean, I'll check the front door before I go to bed, like anyone else, but I don't keep going back to it. It's really just focused on my files and my tools, making sure I haven't lost anything important.
When you check the boxes or drawers repeatedly, does it feel like you have to do it to prevent something bad from happening, or does it help you feel less anxious, even if just for a short time?

Well, I suppose it's more about settling my mind... feeling less anxious, like you said. What really brought me in to see you is that I just find myself checking the exact same boxes, my lists, the drawers around the condo, just over and over before I can move on to whatever I'm supposed to be doing. 

I know perfectly well I already looked. I know I did. But I just have to look again to get that quick relief. It's frustrating, honestly, especially when my wife is standing right there waiting for me to just leave it be so we can go. But doing it just... it settles that nagging feeling for me, at least for a little while, so I can finally walk away.
Are there any other specific thoughts or actions that trouble you in a similar way to the checking, or is it limited only to concerns about losing important items?

Well, no, I think it's pretty much limited to that. I don't have other kinds of worries like that. 

It's really just... I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I may have accidentally thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box. And even when I tell myself it's highly unlikely that I did that—because I'm usually very organized—the thought just comes right back anyway. It just makes it very hard to settle my mind until I go look.
When you check the boxes or drawers, is it because you feel something bad will happen if you don’t, or is it more about just needing to make sure everything is exactly as it should be?

Like I was saying a bit earlier, I don't really think some disaster is going to happen. It's definitely more about just needing to make sure everything is exactly where it should be. 

That's really the whole reason I came in—I just find myself checking those same boxes, my lists, and the drawers around the condo over and over before I can move on to whatever I'm doing. I know perfectly well I already looked, but I still have to check. It's just hard to stop, even when my wife is standing right there waiting for me to just leave it be.

When you check the boxes or drawers, does it feel like something bad will happen if you don't check, or is it more about reducing that uncomfortable feeling or anxiety you get when you think something might be out of place?

Well, like I mentioned, I don't really think anything terrible is going to happen. It's definitely about getting rid of that uncomfortable feeling. That's the whole reason I'm here, really. I just keep checking those same boxes, my lists, the drawers... over and over. Even when I know I've already looked, and even when my wife is standing right there, waiting for me to stop so we can get on with our day. I just have to do it to get that relief so I can finally move on.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms are limited to recurrent checking behaviors related to concerns about losing important items, accompanied by intrusive, unwanted thoughts about misplacing such items. The checking is performed to alleviate anxiety/distress, and there is no evidence of other obsessive-compulsive dimensions (e.g., contamination, symmetry, harm-related obsessions or compulsions). This aligns with the ICD-10 code F42.2 (Mixed obsessional thoughts and acts). Other subtypes such as F42.0 (Predominantly obsessional thoughts) and F42.1 (Predominantly compulsive acts) have been ruled out due to the presence of both obsessions and compulsions, making F42.2 the most accurate diagnosis.
